connect resolves hosted placement through `entire repo view --json`
(entireio/cli#2758), so a host CLI from before that command fails with
unknown-command noise. Gate the placement shell-out on the CLI's reported

existing-binding reconnect fallback never check the host CLI version.
Dev builds, unparseable version lines, and a missing CLI pass through —
the repo view call itself stays the authority on command support.

minHostCLIVersion is "0.0.0" (inert) until the CLI release cuts; plug in
the released version number before shipping.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Trail is set up on `require-cli-version-connect`, committed as `f7f052a6`. Tomorrow you only edit one line: `minHostCLIVersion` in `internal/cli/connect_cmd.go:12` — it's `"0.0.0"` now, which keeps the gate inert until you plug in the release number.

How it works, matching your conditional requirement:

- The check lives inside `resolveHostedPlacement`, the only place brain shells out to `entire repo view --json`. It is connect-only by construction: local brain use never checks, and neither does `connect --repo-id/--api-url` or the reconnect-from-existing-binding fallback.
- Before running `repo view`, it runs `entire version`, parses the `Entire CLI X.Y.Z` line, and refuses anything below the minimum with "upgrade the entire CLI and re-run connect" instead of repo view's unknown-command error.
- Dev builds, unparseable version lines, and a missing CLI pass through — `repo view` itself stays the authority there, so your own dev CLIs won't get blocked.
- Comparison uses `golang.org/x/mod/semver`, already pinned in go.sum (promoted to a direct require, no new download).
